goal: A polished playable sequence that proves the core fantasy: the game remembers the player's rule and turns it back on them.

gates.criterion: Loads from static hosting with no backend and exposes a clear Begin action.
Primary path works at phone portrait and desktop widths without clipped controls.
Trolley, two track outcomes, five people, one person and lever are visually legible.
Pull and do-nothing choices are large, keyboard reachable and touch friendly.
Choice causes a visible animated consequence before reflective text appears.
Player can choose why they acted without philosopher labels.
Rationale creates Rule 01 through the pure moral engine.
Rule 01 remains visibly available and is not merely decorative text.
Bridge case presents the same 1-versus-5 arithmetic with a different causal mechanism.
Rule 01 predicts an action for the bridge before the player chooses.
If the player refuses the predicted action, engine records a contradiction and presentation explicitly compares prior and current choices.
If the player follows the prediction, game acknowledges consistency and presents a harder next stress test rather than dead-ending.
Contradiction path asks what changed and records the selected moral distinction.
At least one distinction triggers a case mutation that removes or isolates that variable.
Current run can survive accidental refresh through client-side persistence and can be deliberately reset.
Reduced-motion preference preserves causal feedback without large camera motion.
Pure moral engine passes automated tests for rule creation, prediction, contradiction and distinctions.
All JavaScript modules pass Node syntax checks.
Golden path produces no uncaught browser errors.
Human evaluator rates the rule-coming-back moment at least 4/5 for impact.
Human evaluator rates desire to continue at least 4/5.
